role: Director of employee affairs (personnel), Ministry of Education
description: According to his official biography he worked from 1957 as director of employee affairs at Qatar's Ministry of Education, a position he used to find jobs for other Palestinian refugees, before becoming fully involved in the national movement in 1970; Wikipedia describes the post as director of personnel in the emirate's civil service. While in Qatar he was recruited to Fatah (1961, according to Britannica and Wikipedia) and raised funds among Palestinians in the Gulf.

role: Founding-generation member of Fatah; member of its Central Committee
description: Britannica states that Yasser Arafat recruited him in 1961 as one of the early key members of Fatah, which came to dominate the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO). His official biography lists him as a member of Fatah's central leadership from 1964 to the present.

role: Head of the PLO's National and International Relations Department
description: His official biography gives 1984–2000 for this post; Britannica dates his leadership of the PLO's international department to the late 1970s and credits him with forging the PLO's first contacts with Israeli peace groups, a strategy the official biography says he initiated in 1974 with the approval of the Palestinian National Council. He also headed a Palestinian-Jordanian committee in 1979–1981 (official biography).

role: Head of the PLO's negotiations portfolio (Negotiations Department); chief architect of the Oslo channel
description: His official biography lists him as head of the PLO Negotiations Department from 1974 to 2003. According to Britannica he shaped Palestinian negotiating strategy at the 1991 Madrid conference and in the secret talks in Norway; he signed the Oslo I Declaration of Principles for the PLO at the White House on 13 September 1993 and, according to his official biography, the Oslo II Interim Agreement in Washington in September 1995. He was a senior member of the Palestinian delegation at Camp David in July 2000.

role: Head of the Palestinian Central Election Committee
organization: Palestine Liberation Organization / Palestinian National Authority
description: Listed in his official biography as head of the Palestinian Central Election Committee from 1996 to 2002, the period of the first general elections of January 1996.

role: Secretary-General of the PLO Executive Committee
description: Listed in his official biography as Secretary-General of the PLO from 1996 to 2004, making him Arafat's number two in the organisation.

role: Prime Minister of the Palestinian National Authority (first holder of the office)
description: Appointed by Yasser Arafat on 19 March 2003 under international pressure, at a time when Israel and the United States refused to negotiate with Arafat. According to Britannica he denounced terrorism, called for an end to the second intifada and sought a single Palestinian armed force, but came into a power struggle with Arafat over control of the security services. He resigned on 6 September 2003, citing a lack of support from Israel and the United States and 'internal incitement' against his government (Britannica; Wikipedia, citing CNN and AP).

role: Chairman of the PLO Executive Committee
description: Named head of the PLO after Yasser Arafat's death on 11 November 2004 (Britannica); Wikipedia dates his assumption of the chairmanship to 29 October 2004, when Arafat was flown to France for treatment. He announced his resignation from the Executive Committee in August 2015 and called an emergency session of the Palestinian National Council, which was postponed; he remained chairman. In April 2025 the PLO created the post of vice-chairman (also styled vice-president of the State of Palestine), to which he appointed Hussein al-Sheikh.

role: President of the Palestinian National Authority
description: Elected on 9 January 2005 for a four-year term and sworn in in Ramallah on 15 January 2005. After the term expired in January 2009 he remained in office: Fatah argued that presidential and legislative elections had to be held together, the PLO Central Council extended his mandate in December 2009 until elections are held, and Hamas disputed the extension. Since the June 2007 Fatah–Hamas split, PA rule has been limited to the parts of the West Bank under its administration; he has governed by decree-law since the Legislative Council stopped meeting in 2007. As of 22 October 2026 he remains president, with the next presidential election set for 11 September 2027.

role: President of the State of Palestine
description: The PLO Central Council chose him as President of the State of Palestine (the state proclaimed by the PLO in 1988) on 23 November 2008, according to Wikipedia; his official biography dates the Central Council vote to 14 October 2008. Since the 2012 UN General Assembly vote granting Palestine non-member observer state status, the PA has used the name 'State of Palestine' officially.

Elected chairman of Fatah at its sixth general conference in 2009 (Wikipedia; his official biography dates his leadership of Fatah from 2004), re-elected unanimously at the seventh conference in Ramallah on 29 November 2016 and at the eighth conference on 14 May 2026.

role: Chair of the Group of 77 at the United Nations (on behalf of the State of Palestine)
description: In January 2019 he accepted, on behalf of Palestine, a UN non-member observer state, the one-year chairmanship of the Group of 77, a coalition of 134 mainly developing countries and China, taking over from Egypt.
